items.q: In a patient presenting with newly identified hypothyroidism, autoantibody screening returns completely negative. What diagnostic entity is considered on page 908?
opts: Transient hypothyroidism due to thyroiditis (postviral or post-vaccine)
items.exp: In the workup for Hashimoto's, negative autoantibodies indicate: 'Transient Hypothyroidism : Thyroiditis (Postviral / Post vaccine) -> may/may not require treatment'. (Book p908)

items.q: Match the autoantibody in Hashimoto's disease to its percentage association on page 908 — 1) Thyroid peroxidase (TPO) antibody 2) Thyroglobulin antibody 3) TSH Receptor Antibody … A) 90 - 100% B) 80 - 90% C) 10 - 20%
items.exp: Autoantibody associations in Hashimoto's: TPO Ab 90 - 100%, Thyroglobulin Ab 80 - 90%, and TSH Receptor Ab 10 - 20%. (Book p908)

items.q: The single most sensitive and prevalent autoantibody in Hashimoto's disease is ___, present in ___ of cases.
items.exp: Thyroid peroxidase antibody is the most strongly associated antibody, present in 90 - 100% of Hashimoto's patients. (Book p908)

items.q: Match the combination of elevated TSH (↑ TSH) and free T4 level to the diagnosis — 1) ↓ Free T4 2) ↑ Free T4 3) Normal Free T4 … A) 1° Hypothyroidism B) TSH Secreting Adenoma C) Subclinical 1° Hypothyroidism
items.exp: ↑ TSH + ↓ Free T4 = 1° Hypothyroidism; ↑ TSH + ↑ Free T4 = TSH Secreting Adenoma; ↑ TSH + Normal Free T4 = Subclinical 1° Hypothyroidism. (Book p908)

items.q: What is the definitive TSH cut-off value that provides an absolute indication for L-thyroxine treatment in confirmed Hashimoto's disease regardless of symptoms?
items.exp: Under Treatment Indications: 'Confirmed Hashimoto's (TSH value > 10 mcu/ltr)'. (Book p908)

items.q: For patients with a TSH value between 5 and 10 mcu/ltr: I Treatment is indicated if vague symptoms are present with TPO positivity, positive family history, or pregnancy. II Treatment is indicated if severe symptoms are present.
opts: Both I and II are true
I is true; II is false
I is false; II is true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: When TSH is 5 - 10 mcu/ltr, treatment is indicated for vague symptoms + (TPO +ve, Family history, Pregnancy) or severe symptoms. (Book p908)

items.q: A 27-year-old woman in early pregnancy is found to have a TSH of 6.8 mcu/ltr with normal free T4. Her anti-TPO antibody titre is elevated. What is the correct management per page 908?
opts: Defer treatment and recheck TSH postpartum
Wait until TSH exceeds 10 mcu/ltr before treating
items.exp: In pregnancy with TSH 5 - 10 mcu/ltr and TPO positivity, L-thyroxine treatment is explicitly indicated. (Book p908)

items.q: What is the recommended starting dose of L-thyroxine for a symptomatic hypothyroid patient under 60 years of age?
In patients under 60 years of age on L-thyroxine, subsequent dosage adjustments should be titrated by ___ µg/day.
items.exp: Under drugs: 'Dose change can be by 25-50 µg/day' for patients under 60 years. (Book p908)

items.q: In elderly patients (> 60 years of age), what is the recommended starting dose and dose adjustment step for L-thyroxine?
opts: Starting dose 25 µg/day; dose change by 25 µg/day
Starting dose 50 µg/day; dose change by 50 µg/day
Starting dose 100 µg/day; dose change by 25 µg/day
Starting dose 10 µg/day; dose change by 5 µg/day
items.exp: In elderly (>60 yr): starting dose is '25 µg/day' and 'Dose change by 25 µg/day'. (Book p908)

items.q: Why must elderly patients (> 60 years) be started on a low dose of L-thyroxine (25 µg/day)?
opts: Due to the risk of cardiotoxicity (e.g., precipitating angina or arrhythmias)
Because of rapid hepatic clearance of levothyroxine in older adults
Due to the high risk of nephrogenic diabetes insipidus
Because older patients do not convert T4 to T3
items.exp: Elderly patients start at 25 µg/day explicitly '(Due to cardiotoxicity)'. (Book p908)

items.q: Which of the following is NOT an indication to treat subclinical hypothyroidism with TSH 5 - 10 mcu/ltr on page 908?
opts: Vague symptoms with a positive family history
Pregnancy or presence of severe symptoms
items.exp: Indications for TSH 5-10 mcu/ltr are: vague symptoms + TPO +ve, family history, pregnancy, or severe symptoms. (Book p908)
